def clean_string(s):
    if s is None:
        return ""
    return str(s).replace("\xa0", " ").strip()

def parse_date_from_text(text):
    """
    Extract the first recognizable date from a string and return a Python datetime.
    Handles common embedded date formats such as:
    dd.mm.yy, dd.mm.yyyy, dd/mm/yy, yyyy-mm-dd, etc.
    """
    text = clean_string(text)
    if not text:
        return None

    patterns = [
        # dd.mm.yy / dd-mm-yyyy / dd/mm/yy
        r'(?<!\d)(\d{1,2})[.\-/](\d{1,2})[.\-/](\d{2,4})(?!\d)',
        # yyyy.mm.dd / yyyy-mm-dd / yyyy/mm/dd
        r'(?<!\d)(\d{4})[.\-/](\d{1,2})[.\-/](\d{1,2})(?!\d)',
    ]

    for idx, pattern in enumerate(patterns):
        match = re.search(pattern, text)
        if not match:
            continue

        nums = [int(x) for x in match.groups()]

        if idx == 0:
            day, month, year = nums
        else:
            year, month, day = nums

        if year < 100:
            year += 2000 if year <= 69 else 1900

        try:
            return datetime(year, month, day)
        except ValueError:
            continue

    return None

# Fill only the exact answer range E6:E19, deriving each value from the same row in column D.

    target = ws.cell(row=row, column=5)

    if result is None:
        target.value = None
    else:
        target.value = result
        target.number_format = "yyyy-mm-dd"

output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
wb.save(output_path)
